blocks.text: Beyond Visible Image Sensor R&D Engineer
SWIR · X-ray · Nanophotonics · Sensor Characterization · Imaging Systems
I study beyond-visible information through optoelectronic sensors.
Mr role is to characterize sensor behavior, analyze performance limits, and provide design directions for the next sensor or system iteration.

Humans perceive the intensity of wavelength from 400nm to 700nm as visible image, and this visual information significantly influences  recognition both on biological and intelligent systems. Based on such stimuli, they react and predict future states. Although the visible provides abundant data, electromagnetic waves possess many other parameters, and these would be valuable as X-Ray did.
My research focuses on extracting and interpreting useful information beyond human vision through electromagnetic sensing systems.

title: Research Approach: Characterization → Analysis → Understand Physics → Design Direction

blocks.text: In beyond-visible sensor research, my role is to characterize sensor behavior, analyze the underlying performance limits, and provide design directions for the next device or system iteration.
I use automated characterization workflows not as an end goal, but as a research tool to connect device-level physics with imaging-system performance.
Python-based sensor characterization and analysis platforms
- GUI development using PyQt and tkinter
- Automated control of source meters, DAQ units, monochromators, spectrometers, and probe stations
- Extraction of sensor metrics: Dark current, EQE, responsivity, detectivity, time response, temporal noise, SNR, DSNU, PRNU, DCR, PDP, and MTF
- Used automated characterization results to identify sensor formance bottlenecks and guide device & system design directions
